time.desc: The navy of one side issues the latest safety guidelines for merchant ship passage in key straits and maintains port blockade measures
The leader of one side publicly accused the other of violating existing ceasefire arrangements and warned of consequences without specifying the details.
For the first time, a leader of one side publicly listed the other side's regime change as a policy goal and issued a tough warning on negotiations and nuclear issues.

Indirect negotiations at the technical level between the two sides were officially launched. On the same day, the other side held a live-fire military exercise in the direction of the key strait and briefly announced the closure of the channel.
The mediating party publicly stated that an agreement between the two parties was close to being reached and emphasized that political will exists.

The two parties launched large-scale joint air strikes against the target country and escalated the confrontation into an open war. The first round of strikes resulted in the death of the other party's top leader, which was officially confirmed.
For the first time, the troop contributor publicly reported that soldiers were killed after the war started and disclosed that they were caused by drone counterattacks.
The target country officially confirms that the top leader will be replaced by a member of his family during wartime
The sending troops launched air strikes on the target country’s main crude oil export hub and attacked its air defense and naval facilities.
A senior financial official from one side made a clear statement on the passage of key straits and directly linked the energy market response to the duration of the conflict.

The coalition's air strikes on energy infrastructure such as world-class natural gas fields have caused significant fluctuations in oil prices, and the troops sending troops said the war will end soon.
The leader of the troop-contributing side issued a time-limited ultimatum on the resumption of navigation in key straits and threatened to attack the other side's power and other infrastructure.
Troop contributors announced that they have entered into dialogue with their opponents and promised to temporarily suspend military strikes on their energy facilities to open a diplomatic window.
The troop-sending party formally submits a conflict-ending plan containing multiple clauses to the opponent as a negotiation text.
The opponent completed a formal reply to a number of ceasefire clauses, bringing the ceasefire negotiations into a new stage.
Major powers and partners outside the region jointly proposed an alternative five-point plan to end the war and called for an immediate ceasefire and the restoration of normal traffic in key straits.

The leader of the troop-contributing party issued a nationally televised speech, saying that he would carry out harsher attacks on his opponents within weeks and reiterated his intention to end the conflict in the short term.
One party deployed an anti-drone laser system near its own city and temporarily closed the airspace.
The media revealed that one government is internally discussing plans to launch a military strike on the other party's nuclear facilities.
The attacked party continued to launch multiple waves of missile and drone offensives against its opponents, and denied the claim that it had 'closed the key strait'

Security sources from the initiating party admitted for the first time that there was no feasible plan for regime change at the beginning of the war, and the whereabouts of large amounts of highly enriched uranium became the key to the outcome of the war.

The leader of the party that launched the attack publicly questioned the life and death of the new supreme leader of the party that was attacked. The president of the party that was attacked issued an open letter calling for negotiations but refused to give in under pressure.
